Learned counsel for the petitioners has filed a memo stating that the first petitioner is the husband and second respondent is the wife and the complaint has been lodged by respondent No.2.

The couple have amicably settled the matter before the Court of VI Additional District and Sessions Judge, Bengaluru Rural District, Bengaluru, in M.C.No.74 of 2020.

entities.text: Additional District and Sessions Judge, Bengaluru Rural District, Bengaluru
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: The second respondent has received Rs.52,50,000/- (Rupees Fifty Two Lakhs Fifty Thousand Only) and two sites from the first petitioner towards permanent alimony and accordingly the marriage between first petitioner and second respondent was dissolved by the judgment and decree dated 15.03.2025.

A copy of the Memorandum of Settlement drawn under Section 89 of CPC read with Rules 24 and 25 of the Karnataka Civil Procedure (Mediation) Rules, 2005, before the Mediation Centre is enclosed along with the memo and a copy of the NC: 2025:KHC-D:7354 HC-KAR judgment and decree passed in M.C.No.74 of 2020 is also filed along with the memo.
3.

As seen from Paragraph No.10 of the Memorandum of Settlement, second respondent herein has agreed to co-operate to quash/closure of C.C.No.625 of 2021, which is the subject matter of this criminal petition.

The learned VI Additional District and Session Judge, Bengaluru Rural District,
has also recorded in Paragraph No.48 of the judgment that the terms of settlement was also complied by the first petitioner herein and is admitted by the second respondent herein.
